thresholdDisclosure.note: BN254 verifier for the threshold (range) disclosure circuit — prove amount <= threshold WITHOUT revealing the amount. Now BOUND THROUGH THE POOL: pool.disclose_threshold(commitment, threshold, ctx, proof) checks the commitment is a known on-chain deposit before verifying, and routes to this verifier (set via admin set_threshold_verifier). So the regulator's range attestation is tied to a real deposit, not a free-floating proof. Soundness: npm run test:threshold 4/4; unit tests disclose_threshold_binds_known_commitment/_rejects_unknown_commitment/_requires_verifier_set. Live-verified: real range proof verifies true on-chain.

aggregateDisclosure.note: BN254 verifier for the COMPLETE VARIABLE-COUNT AGGREGATE (portfolio) disclosure circuit — prove the SUM of 1..5 confidential payments is <= a reporting cap WITHOUT revealing any amount (a periodic CTR report in ZK). Variable count via public per-slot `active` flags (active slot opens its commitment + contributes; inactive is padding). COMPLETENESS ENFORCED ON-CHAIN via an audit-request REGISTRY: (1) circuit binds auditContextHash === Poseidon(ctxNonce, commitments, active) to the exact set, and (2) the AUDITOR role registers that hash on-chain (register_audit_request, auditor-only) for the FULL required set; disclose_aggregate REJECTS any auditContextHash that isn't registered (UnknownAuditRequest #15). So a holder can't mint their own hash for a cherry-picked subset — it isn't registered. Completeness holds when the auditor is an independent regulator; the demo sets the auditor role to the demo key (set_auditor) so the no-install flow can register (every demo role is one person). pool.disclose_aggregate(commitments[5], active[5], cap, ctx, ctxNonce, proof) also requires every ACTIVE slot's commitment to be a known deposit (#3), exactly 5 slots (#13), flags in {0,1}, >=1 active. Soundness: npm run test:aggregate 6/6; unit tests disclose_aggregate_rejects_unregistered_request (#15) + set_auditor_requires_admin. Multi-party ceremony key. Live-verified on-chain.

rangeDisclosure.note: BN254 verifier for the TWO-SIDED RANGE (band) disclosure circuit — prove lower <= amount <= upper (the payment is in a reportable bracket) WITHOUT revealing the amount. Bound through the pool: pool.disclose_range(commitment, lower, upper, ctx, proof) checks the commitment is a known on-chain deposit, then routes to this verifier (set via admin set_range_verifier). Same commitment scheme Poseidon(amount, pubKey, blinding). Soundness: npm run test:range 5/5 (in-band proves, boundaries inclusive, below/above unprovable, wrong-opening unprovable). Unit tests disclose_range_binds_known_commitment/_rejects_unknown_commitment/_requires_verifier_set. Multi-party ceremony key.

reserves.description: REAL cryptographic proof-of-reserves — ADDITIVE, reads the LIVE pool read-only (touches none of the 8 live contracts). __constructor(admin, pool, reserves_verifier). attest(proof, declared_liabilities: i128) reads the pool's balance() + leaves() CROSS-CONTRACT, REBUILDS the verifier public-input vector FROM the on-chain leaves itself (binding discipline: [commitments(32), declaredLiabilities], unused slots padded with the constant Poseidon(0,0,0)), verifies a Groth16 proof (via the pool's trap+assert verify pattern) that the note openings sum to declared_liabilities, panics Insolvent (#2) if declared_liabilities > balance, then stores + emits a timestamped Attestation{liabilities,reserves,timestamp}. Views latest_attestation() -> Option<Attestation>, is_solvent() -> bool, plus pool()/verifier()/admin(). This contractId points at the LIVE pool (verified: pool()=CBIYQACY..., verifier()=CBCVFPJB...); its latest_attestation() is currently null because the live pool's 31 notes are DEPOSITOR-held, so their openings aren't ours to prove (the correct privacy property) — posting a live-pool attestation needs the operator's note-opening witnesses.
reserves.ponytailCeiling: The whole leaf set is treated as obligations, which OVER-counts already-spent notes (a spent note still has a leaf). This only OVER-states liabilities, so passing declared_liabilities <= reserves is conservative (fail-safe). Upgrade path: subtract spent notes via the pool's is_nullifier_used before summing. Also N=32 is a fixed circuit width (covers the live pool's current 31 leaves); a fuller pool needs a bigger ptau or batched/recursive attestation.

Output ceremony/reserves/* (reserves_final.zkey byte-identical to circuits/build/reserves_final.zkey; the deployed verifier embeds the matching VK). Transcript ceremony/reserves/TRANSCRIPT.txt.

reservesAggregate.description: VOLUNTARY, NO-REDEPLOY proof-of-reserves. ADDITIVE and read-only over the live pool (touches none of the 8 live contracts). REUSES the already-deployed aggregate-disclosure verifier (CCTN437J...) — no new circuit, no new ceremony. WHY it exists next to the full-pool reserves contract (CCMIHWMV...): that one needs ALL 31 depositors' note openings at once, which Tukar cannot hold (the notes are depositor-held — that IS the privacy property). The voluntary alternative: each depositor proves a sum over THEIR OWN notes into a shared reserves round using the EXISTING aggregate circuit (prove sum <= cap without revealing any amount), with cap = the depositor's disclosed_sum. __constructor(admin, pool, aggregate_verifier). open_round(ctx_nonce) (admin-only) opens a round with a public context nonce depositors build their proofs against. attest_partial(proof, commitments[5], active[5], disclosed_sum, audit_context) rebuilds the aggregate verifier's 13-input public vector ON-CHAIN in the exact circuit order [commitments(5), active(5), cap=disclosed_sum, auditContextHash, ctxNonce] — the SAME binding discipline the pool's disclose_aggregate uses (audit_context is caller-supplied but PROOF-BOUND: the circuit enforces auditContextHash == Poseidon(ctxNonce, commitments, active) and the contract fixes ctxNonce to the round nonce, so a wrong hash fails verification); requires every ACTIVE commitment to be a real on-chain leaf via pool.is_commitment_known (cross-contract); rejects any commitment already covered this round (per-round covered set keyed by (round, commitment), no double-count -> AlreadyCovered #4); verifies via the aggregate verifier (trap+assert); then accumulates disclosed_sum into the running proven-liabilities total and marks the commitments covered. Views: proven_liabilities() -> i128, covered_count() -> u32, pool_leaf_count() (reads pool), pool_balance() (reads pool), solvent_for_covered() -> bool (proven_liabilities <= balance), round(), ctx_nonce(), plus admin()/pool()/verifier(). This contractId points at the LIVE pool: verified live pool_leaf_count()=31, pool_balance()=50600000000 (506 USDC), round()=1 (open), proven_liabilities()=0, covered_count()=0, solvent_for_covered()=true — an HONEST voluntary lower bound that grows as depositors opt in.
reservesAggregate.ponytailCeiling: Proves solvency for the COVERED subset only (voluntary), so proven_liabilities is a LOWER bound on the pool's true total liabilities — it grows as more depositors attest but never claims to cover the whole pool. Each depositor's contribution is an UPPER bound on their own notes (cap = disclosed_sum), which makes the proven_liabilities <= balance check conservative (fail-safe) for the covered set. Honest partial by design. Full-pool PoR without holding every opening needs the homomorphic-accumulator upgrade (accumulate proven sums under a commitment, not a plain i128).

poolAccumulator (FULL-POOL proof-of-rese.whatItAdds: REAL FULL-POOL cryptographic proof-of-reserves. Byte-identical to contracts/pool-enforced/ EXCEPT: (1) DataKey::TotalLiabilities — a running on-chain field accumulator; (2) deposit folds the SAME `amount` it pulled in AND that the disclosure binding proof proved equals the note commitment's hidden value (TotalLiabilities += amount) via checked_add (Overflow #19); (3) views total_liabilities() -> i128, is_solvent() -> bool (total <= balance), attest_reserves() -> Attestation{liabilities,reserves,timestamp} which panics Insolvent (#18) unless total_liabilities <= balance() then records+emits, and latest_attestation() -> Option<Attestation>.
poolAccumulator (FULL-POOL proof-of-rese.whySound: The construction the full-pool reserves contract (CCMIHWMV...) could not achieve: it needs EVERY depositor's note opening at once (which Tukar cannot hold — notes are depositor-held, the privacy property). Here the ZK work is front-loaded to DEPOSIT time: each deposit already carries the disclosure binding proof (commitment == Poseidon(amount, pubKey, blinding), amount public), so the amount folded into the accumulator is provably the note's amount AND the real token amount moved in — a depositor can neither inflate nor understate. The accumulated total therefore equals the true sum of deposited note amounts, and attest_reserves needs NO opening at read time. Deposit amounts are already public (token transfer + binding proof), so a public field accumulator is equally sound as a hiding Pedersen commitment for a public total — no new circuit/ceremony required.
poolAccumulator (FULL-POOL proof-of-rese.ponytailCeiling: DEPOSIT-SIDE ONLY: it does not subtract a note's amount on withdraw/transfer, so after withdrawals TotalLiabilities OVER-STATES true liabilities. That is the FAIL-SAFE direction — total_liabilities <= custody passing means true_liabilities <= total <= custody (genuinely solvent), so a PASS is strictly conservative (matches contracts/reserves/'s ceiling). A post-withdrawal FAIL can be a false alarm. Also import_state imports leaves without amounts, so it does NOT populate the accumulator — attest_reserves is sound only on a FRESH deposits-from-genesis instance. Upgrade path (deliberately NOT done — invasive to the core transfer/withdraw circuit): fold -amount into the accumulator inside the withdraw/transfer circuit for exact live liabilities.

pool.description: Hardened corridor pool with token custody + FULLY TRUSTLESS tree updates (no admin root backdoor — the only way to advance the root is a merkleUpdate proof). Builds the verifier public inputs from typed signals so nullifiers/commitments/root/amount are BOUND to the proof; root registry + nullifier set + commitment set (idempotent, no double-count) + pinned ASP allow/deny; pulls/releases real tokens on deposit/withdraw.

fxOracle.partner: Reflector — Stellar's decentralized SEP-40 FX oracle (testnet, base = USD)
fxOracle.usedBy: pool.offramp_quote(symbol, usdc_amount) cross-contract-reads lastprice/decimals; verified LIVE: offramp_quote('MXN', 500) returned 8768 = 500 * 17.54 (the live on-chain MXN rate). The frontend reveal calls this contract fn, so the receiver's fiat figure is computed on-chain by the pool reading Reflector.

tested.deposit: success — compliance proof bound to commitment; pulled 100 tokens into the pool (balance 0 -> 100)
tested.withdraw: success — released tokens; publicAmount is NEGATIVE (r - amount: value leaving the shielded set, the correct JoinSplit sign), and the pool binds the released amount to that field-negative so it cannot release more than the proof authorizes. Now also takes an OPTIONAL min-receive gate (offramp_symbol + min_local_out): see minReceiveGate below.
tested.gaslessFeeBump: NATIVE GASLESS (the no-gated-dependency alternative to a Launchtube paymaster): Stellar's CAP-15 fee-bump transactions let a relayer pay the network fee for a tx authorized + signed by another account — same value as Launchtube (user needs no XLM) but a native protocol feature, no gated API token. Since fee-bump is an envelope around any inner tx, it applies unchanged to the corridor's Soroban deposit/withdraw invokes. PROVEN LIVE on testnet (scripts/feebump-paymaster.mjs, npm run demo:feebump): a tx signed by the demo key had its entire fee paid by a fresh paymaster account — paymasterPaidXlm 0.00002, signerDeltaXlm 0 (signer paid nothing). Example tx ef9c15065b469e648839dc56639f8712fc029d450c59b188b3c7f434bc06a6a6. Wiring it as the default Freighter fee sponsor is a small step on the verified primitive but, like Freighter signing, needs a human to exercise end-to-end. See docs/ALTERNATIVES.md for the full alternatives analysis (Mercury obviated by durable-state reconstruction; passkey/SEP-24 gated on a human authenticator / KYC partner).
tested.eventsIndexing: INDEXING TIER (breadth): the pool emits deposit/withdraw/transfer/root events; the frontend reads them back via Stellar RPC getEvents (stellar.js readRecentActivity -> a live 'corridor activity' feed in the console). Verified LIVE on this pool: the feed renders the real on-chain events (deposit, tree-advance, off-ramp withdrawal) with stellar.expert tx links. Privacy holds — deposit/withdraw are the PUBLIC on/off-ramp edges (real USDC moves to/from a public address there); the shielded middle leg is unlinkable and an event feed never reveals which deposit a withdrawal came from. Honest ceiling: testnet public RPC ages events out (~latest-10k ledgers), so this is a RECENT-activity view, NOT a source of truth — the spendable tree is reconstructed from DURABLE contract state (leaves()/leaf_range), which has no retention dependency. (A production deploy would point this at a Mercury subscription for durable indexing.)
tested.minReceiveGate: DEEP integration (audit opportunity #1 executed): withdraw gains optional offramp_symbol + min_local_out. When BOTH are set, the pool re-reads the Reflector oracle ON-CHAIN at settlement (shared quote_local helper with offramp_quote) and refuses to release if the live local-fiat amount is below the floor -> SlippageExceeded (#12). The check runs AFTER proof verification but BEFORE nullifiers are spent, so a slippage-rejected withdraw burns no nullifier and is retryable when the rate recovers. FAIL-CLOSED: a stale OR absent feed traps into FxUnavailable (#11), so funds never move at an unknown rate — quote_local checks both price>0 AND now-timestamp<=3600s (audit round 5: previously only an ABSENT feed failed closed; a frozen-but-positive price would have been used as live — now fixed and the claim is true). This turns Reflector from a display-only read into LOAD-BEARING for fund movement (opt-in: a normal withdraw passes None/None and never consults the oracle). The frontend wires it for the 3 oracle corridors (MXN/BRL/ARS) with a 1% slippage tolerance (min = floor(live_quote * 0.99)), computing the quote from the SAME floored whole-USDC unit the contract gates on (audit round 5 fix: rounding divergence used to permanently block fractional-USDC withdrawals like $20.50). Unit-tested 4 ways (gate passes when rate meets floor; rejects below floor #12; fails closed on a dead feed #11; rejects a stale feed #11) AND verified LIVE end-to-end: offramp_quote('MXN',500)=8756 on this pool (the on-chain staleness check passes because the live Reflector feed is ~2 min fresh), and a 500-USDC MX withdraw releases on-chain when the live re-read holds above the floor.
tested.registerRootVerified: success — trustless root advance via merkleUpdate proof (oldRoot -> newRoot)
tested.trustlessTreeAttack: registering a FAKE new_root with the real proof -> rejected (InvalidProof, Error #0)
tested.amountBindingFix: withdraw with amount=999 but public_amount=50 -> rejected (AmountNotBound, Error #6)
tested.bindingFix: transfer/withdraw with a valid proof but TAMPERED nullifiers -> rejected (InvalidProof, Error #0): nullifiers are part of the verified public inputs, so a double-spend bypass is impossible
tested.noAdminBackdoor: register_root (admin override) removed — root advances ONLY via register_root_verified with a merkleUpdate proof
tested.idempotentCommitment: deposit then register_root_verified of the same leaf records it once (commitment_count is not double-counted)
tested.globalAccumulator: register_root_verified requires old_root == current_root, so the tree is a single append-only GLOBAL accumulator (not a per-session view); inserting from a stale root is rejected (UnknownRoot). Ordered leaves are stored in DURABLE contract state and read via leaves()/leaf_range(start,count)/leaf_count — any client reconstructs the exact tree from on-chain STATE (paginated, so it scales), reload-safe + multi-user-correct, with NO dependency on RPC event retention. Leaf/root entries get their TTL extended (~31d) on each insert so a long-lived pool stays readable. The frontend re-syncs + auto-retries (3x) on the concurrent-deposit race. Verified live across independent sessions: leaves accumulate 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4, each building on the real current root.
tested.complianceAuthFix: KEY-ON-FROM compliance (audit finding #1 fixed): the compliance circuit's sourceKey is now a PUBLIC input that the pool pins to field(from)=keccak256(from XDR) mod r, and deposit require_auth(from)s. So the proof shows THIS AUTHENTICATED depositor is allow-listed — it can't be forged with someone else's public witness. The allow-list (aspRoot 1df51333...) holds field(approvedKeys); the demo key is approved (index 0) so the no-install demo works; a non-approved key can't deposit (honest ASP behavior). Verified live: deposit only succeeds because the browser's addrField(from) matches the contract's addr_field(from) AND equals the allow-list member. The DENY-LIST now holds field(sanctioned account) using the SAME keccak256(addr XDR) mod r derivation (8 deterministic sanctioned testnet accounts, widened from 4), so the non-membership check is semantically real — a deposit proves field(from) is none of those sanctioned accounts (round-2 audit finding #6 fixed). (Caveat: the shared demo key's secret is public, so the DEMO itself isn't access-controlled — but the architecture is now correct for real-wallet users.)
tested.onChainPoseidon: the pool exposes poseidon_hash(a,b) — a circomlib-compatible Poseidon (t=3) computed ON-CHAIN with BN254 host field ops. Live call poseidon_hash(1,2) returns 0x115cc0f5...4417189a, exactly circomlibjs poseidon([1,2]). Proves Soroban CAN compute the circuit's Poseidon on-chain.
tested.securityHardening: adversarial self-audit (docs/SECURITY.md) -> FIXED: verify() now ASSERTS the verifier's bool (ProofRejected #7 — no fail-open if a verifier returns false instead of trapping); deposit rejects amount >= 2^64 (matches the disclosure 64-bit range, #5); register_root_verified rejects inserts past 2^10 leaves (TreeFull #8); the client withdraw resolves the note's real leaf index from the synced tree, not a stale local index; WITHDRAW RECIPIENT is now BOUND into the proof — withdraw drops the ext_data_hash arg and recomputes keccak256(recipient XDR || public_amount) on-chain, so a withdraw proof+nullifiers can't be replayed to a different recipient (verified live: the withdraw only succeeds because the browser keccak/XDR matches the contract recompute); COMPLIANCE now authenticates the depositor (key-on-from, see complianceAuthFix). The only remaining honest caveat is that the shared demo key's secret is public, so the public demo itself isn't access-controlled — but the design is correct for real-wallet (Freighter) users.
tested.nonCanonicalFieldFix: CRITICAL fix (audit finding C1, was also latent on the prior live pool): soroban-sdk's Bn254Fr::from_bytes REDUCES mod r, so a nullifier n and its re-encodings n+r, n+2r, ... (all distinct 32-byte strings < 2^256 since r ~ 2^254) feed the SAME verifier public input and satisfy the SAME Groth16 proof — but spend_nullifiers keyed the double-spend marker on the RAW caller bytes DataKey::Nullifier(n). So a spent note could be replayed with nullifiers=[n0+r, n1+r] (out_commitments re-encoded to match, ext_data_hash recomputed on-chain from the same recipient+amount): the published proof re-verifies, but has(Nullifier(n0+r)) reads false -> double-spend guard bypassed -> pool drain. FIXED: require_canonical() rejects any caller-supplied field element whose 32 bytes != its own mod-r reduction (NonCanonicalField #14), applied at the chokepoints — transfer_inputs (root + nullifiers + out_commitments, covering transfer AND withdraw), deposit commitment, register_root_verified old_root/new_leaf/new_root, and disclose commitment — so every stored key is canonical and equivalent encodings can't diverge. Regression tests withdraw_rejects_noncanonical_nullifier + deposit_rejects_noncanonical_commitment (#14). Verified LIVE: honest deposit->withdraw->disclose e2e 11/11 on the redeployed pool (canonical inputs pass untouched).
tested.notePersistence: the browser persists its notes (throwaway demo secrets) in localStorage keyed by pool, so a RELOAD restores them; combined with the durable on-chain tree, a deposited note stays withdrawable after closing the tab. Verified live: deposit -> reload -> 'saved payment restored' -> withdraw succeeds.
tested.unbackedLeafDrainFix: CRITICAL fix (audit finding T13): previously `deposit` recorded a commitment + moved tokens in but did NOT insert the leaf; the tree advanced ONLY via the permissionless `register_root_verified`, which accepted ANY `new_leaf`. So an attacker could skip `deposit`, insert a self-made commitment with a valid merkleUpdate proof (which only attests the root math, not backing), and `withdraw` against it — draining other users' deposits (a second variant inserted one deposit's commitment twice -> two nullifiers -> double value). FIXED: `register_root_verified` now requires `new_leaf` to be a commitment already recorded by a real `deposit` (or a transfer/withdraw change-note output) -> UnknownCommitment (#3), and inserts each commitment at most once -> LeafAlreadyInserted (#9). Verified LIVE: an un-deposited leaf insert is rejected on-chain with Error(Contract,#3) BEFORE proof verification.
tested.leafIndexBindingFix: HIGH fix (audit finding T14, griefing DoS): the merkleUpdate circuit's leafIndex was PRIVATE and unconstrained, but the contract stores the leaf at its own LeafCount. So a hand-crafted proof attesting insertion at a DIFFERENT empty index than LeafCount would advance current_root to a tree shape the durable leaves() list can't reproduce — permanently desyncing reconstruction from current_root and bricking the shared global accumulator for ~100 stroops (every honest client would then reconstruct a root that was never registered, so no further deposit could be registered and no note withdrawn). FIXED: leafIndex is now a PUBLIC merkleUpdate input and the pool builds the verifier's public-input vector with leafIndex = its own LeafCount, so the proven insertion index MUST equal the slot the contract stores into. Redeployed the merkleUpdate verifier (4 public inputs) + the pool. Verified LIVE end-to-end: the honest deposit->register->withdraw->disclose flow passes with the new 4-public-input proof (a mismatched-index proof fails Groth16 verification by construction, since the contract supplies LeafCount as the public leafIndex).
tested.duplicateCommitmentFix: MEDIUM fix (audit finding): a second `deposit` to the same commitment used to move tokens in but could never become a second spendable leaf (insert-once), permanently locking those tokens. `deposit` now rejects a commitment that's already recorded -> DuplicateCommitment (#10), before any tokens move. Plus `record_commitment` now bumps the commitment's persistent TTL so a deposited-but-unregistered commitment's backing record can't be archived out from under a later register.
tested.transferInputRangeFix: Defense-in-depth (audit finding): transfer.circom range-checked OUTPUT amounts to 248 bits but not INPUTS. Value conservation sum(in)+publicAmount=sum(out) was sound only via the inductive invariant that every tree leaf commits to a <2^248 amount (deposits 64-bit, outputs 248-bit), so a 2-input sum couldn't wrap the BN254 field. Now each INPUT amount is range-checked to 248 bits too (a zero dummy passes trivially), making wrap-freeness explicit rather than reliant on a cross-component invariant. Public inputs unchanged (7), so only the transfer verifier + zkey/wasm were regenerated (Hermez ptau, 15884 constraints < 2^14) and the verifier redeployed; the pool was redeployed only to point at it. Verified LIVE end-to-end: deposit->register->withdraw->disclose->tamper all pass on the new pool, so the added input checks don't reject valid spends.
tested.transferValueMintFix: CRITICAL fix (audit round-3 finding): the public `transfer` entrypoint verified a JoinSplit proof, spent nullifiers and recorded out_commitments but moved NO tokens and did NOT constrain public_amount. The transfer circuit only enforces sum(in)+publicAmount=sum(out), and zero-amount inputs skip the Merkle membership check — so a proof with two zero-value dummy inputs and public_amount=+X is valid and records a fully-backed output commitment worth X out of nothing. That commitment could then be registered into the tree (it passes the backed-commitment check) and withdrawn for X REAL USDC with no deposit — an unconditional, deposit-free drain of the whole pool. FIXED: `transfer` now requires public_amount == 0 (amount_bytes(0)) -> AmountNotBound (#6); a pure shielded transfer conserves value entirely inside the shielded set, and any external value must go through deposit (positive) or withdraw (negative). Verified: new unit test `transfer_rejects_nonzero_public_amount` (#6) + the honest deposit->register->withdraw->disclose->tamper flow re-verified LIVE end-to-end on the redeployed pool.
tested.nullifierTtlFix: HIGH fix (audit round-3 finding): spent-nullifier markers were `set` with the default persistent TTL and never extended, while leaves and roots ARE continually TTL-extended. On a long-lived pool a nullifier could be archived/evicted while its note stayed provable (leaves/roots refreshed, proof buildable against the current root), so `has(Nullifier)` would read false and the same note could be spent again — a time-delayed double-spend. FIXED: `spend_nullifiers` now extends each nullifier's TTL (TTL_THRESHOLD/TTL_EXTEND) to match the leaf/root TTL, so a spent marker never decays while its note is reachable.
tested.reflectorComposability: DEEP integration (audit opportunity #1 executed): the pool CONTRACT reads the Reflector SEP-40 oracle ON-CHAIN. `offramp_quote(symbol, usdc_amount)` cross-contract-calls Reflector `lastprice(Asset::Other(symbol))` + `decimals()` and returns local = usdc * 10^decimals / price. THREE corridors are oracle-backed (the currencies the testnet feed carries): Mexico MXN, Brazil BRL, Argentina ARS — verified LIVE on-chain on this pool: offramp_quote('MXN',500)=8757, ('BRL',500)=2587, ('ARS',500)=737252, all matching the live rates; the other corridors fall back to a public FX API. The frontend off-ramp reveal calls this fn so the receiver's revealed figure is contract-derived from the partner oracle, not a client hardcode. Turns Reflector from a cosmetic frontend read into load-bearing contract-to-contract composability. A FOLLOW-ON deepening (see minReceiveGate) makes the oracle OPT-IN load-bearing for fund movement too: withdraw can pass offramp_symbol + min_local_out so the pool re-reads Reflector at settlement and refuses to release below the floor.
tested.offrampQuoteEdgeCases: Deep-QA hardening + LIVE negative-path verification on this pool: offramp_quote('JPY',500) (a currency the feed doesn't carry) -> FxUnavailable (#11) [lastprice None]; offramp_quote('MXN', 2^64) -> InvalidAmount (#5) [over-range]; offramp_quote('MXN', 0) -> 0. The fn bounds the amount to the 64-bit deposit range and uses checked_pow/checked_mul, so a malicious/buggy oracle returning a huge `decimals` or an overflow returns a typed FxUnavailable rather than a VM trap. set_fx_oracle is admin-gated (require_auth) with a fx_oracle() view. Two parallel QA subagents (contract + frontend) confirmed offramp_quote is strictly display-only — a bad oracle can never touch custody, withdraw amounts, nullifiers, or the tree.
tested.unitTests: 50/50 pass (adds set_asp_root_updates_view + set_deny_list_updates_view + set_deny_list_rejects_wrong_len [configurable compliance policy — admin can re-point aspRoot/denyList without redeploy, mirrors Confidential Tokens]; withdraw_oracle_gate_median_ignores_spot_outlier + withdraw_oracle_gate_rejects_thin_feed [#11] + offramp_quote_twap_reads_median_on_chain [audit-round-9 manipulation-resistant median gate]; transfer_rejects_shifted_io_split + withdraw_rejects_shifted_io_split [#13 BadIoCount, audit-round-7 CRITICAL double-spend fix]; withdraw_oracle_gate_passes_when_rate_meets_floor, withdraw_oracle_gate_rejects_below_floor [#12], withdraw_oracle_gate_fails_closed_on_dead_feed [#11], withdraw_oracle_gate_rejects_stale_feed [#11, audit round 5] for the min-receive settlement gate; offramp_quote_reads_oracle_on_chain [incl. zero], offramp_quote_unsupported_currency_rejected [#11 via empty-feed mock], offramp_quote_rejects_negative_amount [#5], set_fx_oracle_updates_view; plus poseidon_matches_circomlib, accumulator stale-root rejection, ordered-leaf storage, leaf_range pagination, deposit amount-range guard, register_root_verified_rejects_undeposited_leaf/_double_insert, deposit_rejects_duplicate_commitment, transfer_rejects_nonzero_public_amount; withdraw_rejects_noncanonical_nullifier + deposit_rejects_noncanonical_commitment [#14 NonCanonicalField, audit finding C1 double-spend fix])

poolTimelock (preview, ADMIN TIMELOCK on.closes: docs/THREAT_MODEL.md §3.5 (admin-key compromise) — the last named hardening gap. Before this, every compliance setter was an instant admin.require_auth() write, so a stolen admin key was an INSTANT compliance bypass (re-point the ASP allow-root or deny-list = change who may deposit, or the FX oracle, with no delay). Soroban has no native contract-admin multisig, so the contract-level control is a TIMELOCK; it pairs with running the admin as a Stellar classic MULTISIG account (an account-config step, not code).
poolTimelock (preview, ADMIN TIMELOCK on.timelocked: FIVE setters are now propose -> mandatory delay -> execute -> (cancel), admin-gated: set_asp_root + set_deny_list (the allow/deny controls, the §3.5 core), plus set_fx_oracle, set_auditor, set_policy_registry. Each direct instant setter is REMOVED and replaced by propose_set_X(value) / execute_set_X() / cancel_set_X() / pending_set_X()->Option<(value,eta)>. NOT timelocked (deliberately, out of §3.5 scope): upgrade + import_state stay direct admin calls (import is already one-shot + virgin-only), and the additive disclosure-verifier setters set_threshold_verifier/set_aggregate_verifier/set_range_verifier stay direct — they only enable extra read-only regulator disclosure proofs, are not allow/deny controls, and move no funds.
poolTimelock (preview, ADMIN TIMELOCK on.delayDesign: TIMELOCK_DELAY is stored at construction and read via timelock_delay(). It is a compile-time const (60s on this deploy), NOT a constructor arg: Soroban caps a contract function at 10 inputs and the pool's __constructor already uses all 10, so DELAY cannot be an 11th arg (an 11-input constructor produces a spec the SDK cannot parse — 'saw 11 length VarArray, max allowed is 10'). 60s is intentionally SHORT so the after-eta execute path is demonstrable end-to-end; a PRODUCTION corridor uses a long delay (e.g. 24-48h = 86_400..172_800s), sized against the monitoring window (§5, every propose emits a tl_prop event). propose sets eta = ledger.timestamp() + DELAY; one pending slot per setter (a re-propose overwrites and RESETS the eta to a fresh full delay — no shortcut); execute requires now >= eta else TimelockNotReady (#20); execute/cancel with nothing pending -> TimelockEmpty (#21).

stateMigrationTooling (lossless upgrade.purpose: The LIVE pool CBIYQACY... has NO upgrade hook and NO import-state, so a lossless upgrade means deploying a NEW pool that CAN import the live shielded state, then re-inserting it. contracts/pool-enforced/ is that target: it already has the withdraw cap gate + admin upgrade(new_wasm_hash), and now an admin-only ONE-TIME import_state. NOTHING here touches the 8 live contracts or the live pool — the whole flow is proven against a TEST-DOUBLE source pool with known state.
stateMigrationTooling (lossless upgrade.importState: pool-enforced.import_state(leaves: Vec<BytesN<32>>, root, nullifiers: Vec<BytesN<32>>, asp_root, deny_list[8]) — admin-only (require_auth), ONE-SHOT + virgin-only (refuses if DataKey::Migrated is set OR the pool already has any leaves/commitments -> AlreadyMigrated #17), so it is always the FIRST state-changing call and can never run twice. Re-inserts each leaf at its source index (Commitment backing record + insert-once Inserted guard + ordered Leaf(i) + LeafCount), registers+sets current_root, marks every supplied nullifier used (canonical-checked, dedup via spend_nullifiers, TTL-matched), sets asp_root + deny_list, then seals DataKey::Migrated. Byte-compatible with the existing storage layout, so leaf_count()/current_root() match the source exactly and every migrated spent note stays unspendable. Only the source's CURRENT root is imported (not historical roots); notes re-prove membership against current_root() via the reconstructable leaves() list, the same discipline register_root_verified relies on. is_migrated() view exposes the flag.
stateMigrationTooling (lossless upgrade.nullifierEnumerationFinding: BLOCKING for a BLIND migration, MITIGATED by design. The pool's withdraw/transfer events publish ONLY (withdraw, recipient)->amount and (transfer,)->root — they DO NOT publish nullifiers — and no view enumerates the nullifier set (only is_nullifier_used(n), which needs n up front). So the spent-nullifier set CANNOT be reconstructed from on-chain data (events or views) alone. Consequence: a migration that dropped any spent nullifier would let that already-spent note be re-spent on the new pool (double-spend). MITIGATION: import_state REQUIRES the full nullifier list as an explicit argument (sourced from the operator's own off-chain records), documents loudly that it is correct ONLY when that list is COMPLETE, and cannot verify completeness on-chain. read-pool-state.mjs logs the enumeration method as 'operator-supplied', cross-checks each supplied nullifier against is_nullifier_used, and WARNs that completeness is unverifiable on-chain. (Evidence: contracts/pool/src/lib.rs withdraw ~680 / transfer ~622 publish no nullifiers; only is_nullifier_used ~842 exists.)

Nullifiers are operator-supplied via --nullifiers <file.json> (see finding); it logs the enumeration method + count and WARNs on incompleteness. Importable as { readPoolState }.

onChainPoseidonFinding.claimRevised: Earlier I said on-chain Poseidon was impossible because env.crypto() has no Poseidon host fn. That was wrong: BN254 Fr add/mul/pow host ops are enough to compose circomlib-exact Poseidon on-chain (see pool.poseidon_hash, verified live).
onChainPoseidonFinding.whyTreeStaysProofBased: Measured cost: ONE Poseidon hash = ~13.6M CPU instructions; a depth-10 Merkle insert = 10 hashes ≈ 135M CPU, which EXCEEDS Soroban's ~100M per-transaction budget (and a deposit already spends two Groth16 verifications). So recomputing the tree on-chain per deposit is infeasible — the correct, affordable design is to verify each insert with a merkleUpdate Groth16 proof (one pairing), which register_root_verified already does.
onChainPoseidonFinding.evidence: pool.poseidon_hash + contracts/pool/src/poseidon.rs + the poseidon_matches_circomlib / poseidon_cost_probe unit tests
